entries.title: Writer trial, 'Search From Scratch' (5-part series): Qwen4 Max, Gemini 4 Carbon, Gemini 4 Hydrogen, Kimi K3.1 Pro vs GLM-5.3 (Claude-supervised, impromptu)
entries.judge: claude-opus-5-5 (one subagent per part, not blind; raw drafts judged before any edit)
entries.method: mwp-admin skill writer-trial. Each part dispatched as a pipeline script_only job with the same prompt and host_notes (series hand-offs and 'stay off' fences) per candidate; GLM-5.3 (live writer) drafted every part as the baseline. Verdict per raw draft: pass (airs with light edits) / marginal (airs only with heavy edits) / fail. One challenger draft per part was edited by Claude and aired, credited to the model that wrote it; airing is the human evaluation. Full log (private): monorepo planning/model-review/writer-trials.jsonl and HF My-Weird-Prompts/Evaluations.

summary.qwen/qwen4-max: 5 drafts: pass on Parts 1, 2, 5; marginal on 3, 4. Deepest mechanics and best jokes of the session; runs 1.2-1.5x long; faded on later parts (archive size wrong, wandered into later parts).
summary.google/gemini-4-carbon: 2 drafts: pass (Part 2, cleanest challenger draft), marginal (Part 5: reranker literature where the brief said to place it; arithmetic slips).
summary.google/gemini-4-hydrogen: 1 draft: marginal (Part 4). Sharpest analysis of where brute-force search stops working, but speaker misattribution and a call-in answered before the caller spoke.
summary.moonshotai/kimi-k3.1-pro: 2 drafts: marginal both. Most conceptually sharp, ~1.6x long, recites research tables (Part 3 broke the fusion fence).
summary.z-ai/glm-5.3: 5 drafts (baseline): pass on Parts 1, 4; marginal on 2, 3, 5. Most disciplined on length; least reliable on facts (Part 2 put the archive at ~400 episodes).

findings: No challenger was clearly better than GLM-5.3 overall: livelier and deeper, not cleaner.
Series fences failed for every model: almost every draft drifted into the next parts' material (fusion, reranking, evaluation).
Every Part 4 draft understated the archive's size (~6,700 episodes, ~100-180k chunks), so it misplaced where brute-force search stops working.
Shared tics: Herman quizzing Corn, numbered-episode outro plugs, research mechanics said on air, a recycled card-index monologue for Hilbert.
entries.cost: Draft round about $0.80 across 15 drafts; TTS about $0.10-0.20 GPU per aired episode.
entries.caveats: One prompt per part; one Claude judge, not blind; research differs per run; challengers judged against GLM-5.3's known profile, not a rubric score. Not a ScriptBench score and not comparable with leaderboard.json. Daniel's verdicts (by listening) pending.

entries.title: GLM-5.3 vs Claude Sonnet 5.5 vs Mistral Large 4 vs Gemini 3.8 Flash (blind, Eval-Prompts ep-01/ep-02)
entries.judge: claude-opus-5-5 (blind subagent; letters shuffled per episode)
entries.caveats: Two prompts, one Claude judge (possible Anthropic-house-style bias toward Sonnet). Sonnet samples are the aired scripts; the others are script_only runs with their own research pass, so research differs per run. Guest beats varied.

notes.anthropic/claude-sonnet-5.5: about $0.35-0.37 LLM per aired episode (mwp-script key, traces #2677/#2682)
notes.all three challengers: 6 script_only runs together $0.94 on the supervised-scripts key, all stages included; per-model split pending activity data

impressions.z-ai/glm-5.3: Ranked 2nd on ep-01 and 1st on ep-02. The most evidence-minded writer, with a vivid primary-source day-in-the-life (Cheshire 1662 court depositions) and an opinionated Corn. No Herman quizzing. Weakness: continuity and attribution glitches (lines answering things never said, wrong speaker).
impressions.anthropic/claude-sonnet-5.5: Ranked 1st on ep-01 and 2nd on ep-02. Warm, balanced, the most natural back-and-forth; Corn pushes back. Some hedging and one Herman-quizzes-Corn question on ep-02.
impressions.mistralai/mistral-large-4-0: Ranked 3rd on both. Clipped, natural lines but tutorial-like stretches; Corn often a question feeder; two Herman-quizzes-Corn on ep-02.
impressions.google/gemini-3.8-flash: Last on both. Lecture-like with no contractions, Corn echoing each Herman paragraph as a metaphor, shaky invented details, most slop.

entries.daniel_note: Pending: Daniel to read or hear the scripts.
entries.verdict: GLM-5.3 matched Sonnet 5.5 (one win each) at a fraction of the cost; Mistral Large 4 a clear third; Gemini 3.8 Flash last, consistent with its EQ-Bench slop score.

entries.title: Muse Spark 1.3 vs Claude Sonnet 5.5 vs GPT-6.1 Sol

episodes.note: Claude Code offline-script-writer, voiced by pipeline

entries.caveats: Muse Spark 1.3 wrote three episodes in this window (#6137, #6220, #6229). Every Sonnet 5.5 episode since 2026-10-19 is episode_type=script (offline), so the Sonnet samples had their own research notes and prompt, not the pipeline's. They aren't like for like.

notes.anthropic/claude-sonnet-5.5: offline runs cost subscription, not this

impressions.openai/gpt-6.1-sol: The best of the three. It's the most accurate and the most careful about what a source does and doesn't show ("I'm not giving the beamformer credit for work it may not have done"). It handles a personal health prompt with real judgement. Corn has real agency: he makes analytical points, not just quips. The humour is dry and lands. Weaknesses: the register is a little formal and British ("an appalling interpretation of convenience"), so it's less warm than Sonnet, and Hilbert's cameo monologues ramble.
impressions.meta/muse-spark-1.3: Solid value, clearly a step down. It's dense, factual, on length and cheap. But Corn turns into a quip machine: nearly every Corn line is a three-to-five-word aphorism ("Store an elephant, ride a bicycle", "Death by tapas"). There are speaker slips: in #6229 Corn delivers Herman's research, and Hilbert answers Herman as "Corn". It drops question marks ("Is that roughly right."), which hurts TTS prosody. The Hilbert cameos are its best moments.
impressions.anthropic/claude-sonnet-5.5: The liveliest and warmest, but offline-written. It has the best guest voice (Roy the Cork plumber), a real two-sided argument with the Daniel clone, and natural long turns. Its honest hedging is good, but it slips into narrating research mechanics on air ("I've only seen that in a search snippet"). At OpenRouter prices it costs the same as Sol, so it has no value edge in the pipeline.

entries.impressions_all_models: Every model, so the prompt drives it: formulaic hand-offs ("Corn, would you...?", "Do you buy that, Corn?") and non-sequitur cameo inserts. Don't score these against one model.
entries.daniel: Sol seems very good, no complaints about it.
entries.daniel_note: None given for Muse Spark or Sonnet. He didn't remember which episodes Muse Spark had written, so the lookup above answers that.
entries.verdict: Keep GPT-6.1 Sol as the writer. Muse Spark 1.3 is the fallback if cost pressure appears: about half the price per script, but expect weaker co-host play and TTS-unfriendly punctuation. Sonnet 5.5 is worth it only offline, where its cost is already paid. In the pipeline it costs what Sol costs and isn't better.
